Subject: Urgent: availability tolerance request for Adaptive-Safety preview

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We want to move the Adaptive-Safety preview into a limited production route next week for two pilot hospitals — primary goal is to catch high-severity safety regressions before full rollout. Our engineering and compliance teams understand this is a preview, but they asked whether Redwood can temporarily accept a slightly reduced availability target for the first two weeks (we estimate 95% uptime instead of the standard 99.9%) while we validate behaviour and traffic patterns.

We'd like a written exception or conditional carveout that documents the temporary target, any compensation or rollback triggers, and the mitigation steps Redwood will take (circuit breakers, fallback model, or traffic shifting). Attached is a short summary from our compliance team outlining what they need for audit.

Do you have a quick internal approval path for this? The go/no-go for our pilot is Friday 7/17.

Appreciate a fast turnaround — Eli
Product & Platform, ArborHealth

Subject: Internal: draft provisional carveout for ArborHealth (adaptive-safety)

Team — drafting the carveout language below. Please comment inline; we need sign-off from Marcus (ops) and Laura (runtime) by EOD Thursday.

Draft carveout (summary):
- Scope: Adaptive-Safety alpha-preview (model v0.9) serving only to two ArborHealth hospital endpoints (IDs redacted).
- Duration: 14 calendar days from pilot start (with automatic re-evaluation at day 7).
- Availability target: 95% for pilot window. Redwood will use best-effort routing; outage definitions follow standard prod SLA but with the adjusted target.
- Fallback: On outage or sustained degraded latency, Redwood will route affected requests to the standard safety-tier model and provide per-minute logs.
- Rollback triggers: >5 severity-1 incidents in 24h OR inability to fallback cleanly for 60 consecutive minutes.
- Compensation: pro-rated credits for availability shortfall, capped at 25% of monthly usage during the pilot window.
- Auditables: request-level traces, token-level cost summary, KV-cache logs for the pilot customers (retention 90 days).

Questions/asks for tech:
- Laura: can we ensure KV-cache isolation for pilot routes?
- Marcus: will ops accept the 60-minute fallback window and the monitoring hooks?

Grace
Senior Product, Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 14:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: draft provisional carveout for ArborHealth (adaptive-safety)

Quick technical readout — copied the risk checklist (attached) and a short mitigation plan. High-level:
- KV-cache isolation: feasible with route tags; we'll spin up dedicated cache namespaces for the two hospital routes.
- Fallback model: we recommend a graded fallback — first attempt reroute to safety-tier ML endpoint (latency +0-30ms), second to a simpler heuristic service if the safety-tier experiences sustained faults.
- Monitoring: instrument SLOs at 1m, 5m and 1h windows; add an automated PagerDuty escalation if error rate >2% for 5m.
- Operational constraint: if peak QPS exceeds 12k for a sustained 10m, we will require pre-authorized burst capacity reservation (we can provision same day but need explicit commit).

I attached: adaptive-safety-preview-slo-proposal.pdf (pdf), risk-mitigation-checklist.xlsx (xlsx).

Laura Bennett
Staff Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Urgent: availability tolerance request for Adaptive-Safety preview — provisional carveout approved

Eli — thanks for the patience. We reviewed internally and can approve a provisional availability variance under the following conditions (summarized):

1) Scope & duration: 14-day pilot limited to the two hospital endpoints you identified; pilot start must be confirmed by 10:00 PT on 7/21.
2) Availability: temporary target set to 95% for the pilot window; automatic re-eval at day 7.
3) Technical controls: KV-cache isolation and graded fallback to safety-tier model as described by Laura; automated monitoring and PagerDuty escalation configured.
4) Rollback & triggers: >5 sev-1 incidents in any 24h OR inability to fallback for 60 consecutive minutes => Redwood will pause the pilot and restore routing to safety-tier model.
5) Compensation: pro-rated service credit for availability shortfall, capped at 25% of usage billed for the pilot month.
6) Burst capacity: if ArborHealth anticipates sustained peaks above 12k QPS, pre-authorized burst capacity is required (same-day provisioning possible with signed order).
7) Auditables: Redwood will provide request-level traces, token-cost summaries, and 90-day retention for pilot logs.

Next steps: please reply with (A) confirmation to start 7/21, (B) expected QPS and peak windows, and (C) signed acknowledgement of the carveout terms (I can drop a DocuSign if you prefer).

Attachment: provisional-carveout-text.docx (docx)

If that timeline works we’ll stand up the isolation and monitoring tonight to be ready for a morning start.

Thanks — Karthik
